ref: Diagnose probable acute glaucoma in a patient with eye/vision symptoms
text: Requires ALL of pain, red eye, blurred vision, haloes, fixed dilated pupil AND one of headache/nausea/vomiting. The page lists these as features of a painful red eye; requiring every one (especially haloes and fixed pupil) is likely far too strict, so acute glaucoma would rarely fire.

Single-eye branch ('one eye, no eczema/hayfever/asthma: localised cause likely') is not encoded; the rule only covers the both-eyes/atopy branch. Also the symptom requirement duplicates the itch branch faithfully.

ref: Urgent: eye/vision symptoms with danger signs
text: Acute glaucoma, gonococcal, orbital cellulitis, stroke and jaundice branches depend on diagnoses from rules above (stroke lacks TIA; glaucoma rule too strict), so those danger signs may not fire. Priority itself is justified by the red box heading. Chemical burn lacks eye site. Preeclampsia/postpartum branch uses onset <= 1 week, consistent with briefing convention.
